title: Shortest Path to Get Food
notes:
## Intuition

Every step costs the same, so the fewest steps to any food cell is a shortest path in an unweighted grid graph: exactly what breadth-first search finds. Starting from `'*'`, BFS visits cells in rounds: all cells 1 step away, then all cells 2 steps away, and so on. The first time a round touches a `'#'`, that round number is the answer. If the queue empties first, no food is reachable.

## Approach

1. Scan the grid for `'*'`, put it in `queue` and mark it in `seen`.
2. Process the queue one round at a time: `levelEnd` marks where the current round stops, and `steps` counts rounds.
3. For each cell of the round, look at its four neighbours `(nr, nc)`. Skip ones outside the grid, already `seen`, or `'X'`.
4. If a neighbour is `'#'`, return `steps` right away.
5. Otherwise mark it `seen` and add it to the queue for the next round.
6. If the queue runs out, return `-1`.

## Example 1, step by step

The start is at `(1, 1)` and the only food is at `(2, 3)`. Round 1 (`steps = 1`) reaches `(2, 1)` and `(1, 2)`. Round 2 reaches `(2, 2)` and `(1, 3)`. In round 3 the neighbour `(2, 3)` of `(2, 2)` is `'#'`, so the answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m * n): each cell is queued at most once and checks four neighbours.
- Space: O(m * n) for `seen` and the queue.

## Pitfalls

- Mark a cell `seen` when it is queued, not when it is taken out, or the same cell can be queued many times.
- There may be no food at all, or every food cell may be walled off; both mean `-1`.
- Use an index `head` instead of `queue.shift()`, which costs O(length) per call and makes large grids slow.
- The start is not necessarily surrounded by obstacles, so always check the grid bounds.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | grid dimensions |
| `seen` | cells already queued |
| `queue` | cells waiting to be expanded, as `[r, c]` |
| `head` | index of the next cell to take from `queue` |
| `steps` | distance of the round being generated |
| `levelEnd` | end of the current round in `queue` |
| `nr`, `nc` | the neighbour being examined |
